article.headline: Washington Bets on Pre-Ordering Nuclear Parts to Beat the Clock
article.lede: The U.S. Energy Department is weighing a plan to offer loan guarantees to utilities so they can pre-purchase the most time-consuming nuclear reactor components before construction permits arrive. The goal is to break the supply-chain bottleneck that helped push the country's last large reactor project seven years behind schedule. A cluster of nuclear and uranium stocks sold off sharply the same week — but the policy backstory is arguably more bullish than the price action suggests.
article.body:
The U.S. Department of Energy is weighing a plan to extend loan guarantees to a group of five or six utilities, enabling them to pre-purchase the *long-lead components* of large nuclear reactors — principally *reactor pressure vessels* and steam generators — before those projects have full regulatory approval. These parts take 42 to 54 months to manufacture and can be sourced only at a handful of specialized facilities worldwide, none currently in the United States. By financing the parts queue ahead of permits, the government aims to compress overall build timelines by years.

The move draws directly on lessons from Plant Vogtle, the two **AP1000** reactors completed in Georgia in 2023 and 2024 — the last large commercial units built in the country. Those reactors ran roughly seven years behind their original construction schedule and cost approximately $35 billion against an original estimate of $14 billion, partly because critical components were not ordered until after regulatory milestones arrived. The Nuclear Energy Institute has confirmed that binding term-sheet discussions are underway at the DOE loan office, with a potential $80 billion development program for up to ten new AP1000 units as the broader target. Grant Isaac, president and COO of Cameco (CCJ) — which owns 49% of Westinghouse Electric, the AP1000's designer — has said utilities in advanced talks are “interested in advancing project delivery by considering things like ordering the long lead items ahead of time.”

Against that policy backdrop, the sector absorbed a sharp one-day selloff around May 12 that sent most nuclear and uranium names down 6–12%. The proximate triggers were paired: NuScale Power (SMR) had just reported first-quarter revenue of $565,000 against analyst expectations of $14.8 million — an almost total miss — while Oklo (OKLO) disclosed quarterly losses that had widened to $33.1 million from $7 million a year earlier. A simultaneous U.S.–China tariff truce triggered a *risk-on rotation* in broader markets, pulling capital out of alternative-energy positions. Neither two pre-revenue companies missing forecasts nor a trade deal materially alters the demand thesis for nuclear baseload power.

Cameco (CCJ) reported earnings up 87% year-over-year in its most recent quarter; its Westinghouse stake makes it a direct play on any AP1000 new-build wave. Energy Fuels (UUUU), the largest licensed uranium processor in the United States, posted first-quarter revenue up 112%, selling uranium at $70 per pound. Centrus Energy (LEU) holds the only U.S. license to produce *HALEU* — high-assay low-enriched uranium — the advanced fuel required by next-generation designs including Oklo’s Aurora and X-Energy’s (XE) Xe-100; Centrus enters 2026 with a $3.8 billion revenue backlog extending through 2040. BWX Technologies (BWXT), the only large commercial nuclear equipment manufacturer in North America, signed a manufacturing agreement with Westinghouse in late 2024 specifically for AP1000 and AP300 pressure vessels, and carries a $7.3 billion order backlog.

The less settled question is how long the pre-revenue *microreactor* developers — Oklo (OKLO), NuScale Power (SMR), NANO Nuclear Energy (NNE) — can sustain their current valuations. Oklo’s first Aurora powerhouse broke ground in September 2025, with grid power targeted for 2028; NuScale holds NRC design certification but has no finalized commercial project site; NNE remains in early design review. The DOE long-lead financing plan, if it proceeds, benefits the established AP1000 value chain most directly — uranium miners, enrichers, and component manufacturers. For concept-stage plays, the policy environment is as favorable as it has been in decades; the timeline to revenue is not.

concepts.definition: Critical reactor parts — chiefly reactor pressure vessels and steam generators — whose manufacturing timelines are so long that they must be ordered years before construction begins. For AP1000-scale reactors, lead times run 42–54 months. If a utility waits for regulatory approval before ordering, the delivery date will delay the entire project by exactly that lag.

The heavy steel container that encloses the nuclear fuel core and primary coolant under high pressure and temperature. It is one of the most specialized components in a reactor plant, requiring large-scale precision forging and welding at facilities that exist in only a handful of countries.

A pressurized-water reactor design by Westinghouse Electric rated at roughly 1,100 megawatts of electricity. It is the only large commercial reactor design currently licensed for construction in the United States. Georgia’s Plant Vogtle Units 3 and 4 are the only two AP1000s in commercial operation worldwide.

A government commitment to repay a lender if the borrower defaults, allowing developers to secure financing on better terms than private markets alone would offer. The DOE has used this tool for large energy projects — including Plant Vogtle — under authority granted by the Energy Policy Act of 2005.

A market dynamic in which investors shift capital from defensive or speculative alternative assets toward more cyclical positions in response to improved macro sentiment — such as a trade-war ceasefire. The rotation can cause sharp single-day moves in sectors that had been held as hedges against geopolitical or economic uncertainty.

High-assay low-enriched uranium: uranium enriched to between 5% and 20% uranium-235, compared with the roughly 3–5% used in conventional light-water reactors. Most advanced reactor designs — including small modular reactors and microreactors — require HALEU because their smaller cores need denser fuel to sustain a chain reaction.

A nuclear reactor design producing less than 300 megawatts of electricity, intended to be factory-built in standardized modules and shipped to site. SMRs promise lower upfront capital costs and faster construction than large conventional plants, though very few have yet entered commercial operation.

A nuclear reactor generating under roughly 20 megawatts of electricity, designed for off-grid, remote, or distributed applications such as military bases, data centers, or remote industrial sites. Microreactors are a subset of small modular reactors but are even smaller — some designed to be transportable by truck or aircraft.

Formal approval from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) that a reactor design meets federal safety requirements. A certified design can be referenced in construction permit applications without re-litigating design-level safety questions — a significant regulatory shortcut that can shave years off a project timeline.

ticker_ccj.name: Cameco Corporation
ticker_ccj.blurb: Cameco Corporation is a leading global provider of uranium fuel for nuclear power generation, operating through three segments: Uranium, Fuel Services, and Westinghouse. The Uranium segment explores, mines, and sells uranium concentrate; Fuel Services handles refining, conversion, and fabrication; and Westinghouse is a nuclear reactor technology OEM. Headquartered in Canada, Cameco is one of the world's largest uranium producers and plays a critical role in the nuclear energy supply chain.
ticker_ccj.recent: In the past 30 days, Cameco reported strong earnings on May 5, 2026, with net income surging 161.6% year-over-year to $466.07 million. The stock has traded in a 52-week range of $48.81 to $135.24, closing at $116.75 on May 8, 2026. Analysts maintain a Strong Buy rating with a price target of $123.92, reflecting optimism around nuclear energy demand.

ticker_smr.name: NuScale Power Corporation
ticker_smr.blurb: NuScale Power Corporation designs and commercializes small modular reactor (SMR) technology, centered on its NuScale Power Module (NPM) — a light-water nuclear reactor capable of generating 77 megawatts of electricity per unit. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in the United States, the company provides end-to-end services including regulatory licensing support, design and engineering, construction guidance, and operator training. NuScale holds the distinction of being the first SMR design to receive NRC design approval in the U.S., positioning it as a first-mover in the emerging commercial SMR market. With roughly 428 employees and a pre-revenue scale operation, it remains a development-stage company competing in the industrials/specialty machinery sector.
ticker_smr.recent: NuScale reported earnings on May 7, 2026, with trailing-twelve-month revenue of $18.67M (down ~62% year-over-year) and a net loss of $385.8M, reflecting its continued pre-commercial buildout phase. The stock has declined sharply from its 52-week high of $57.42 to approximately $11.96 as of May 13, 2026 — near the lower half of its annual range of $8.85–$57.42 — amid investor reassessment of SMR commercialization timelines. Analyst consensus sits at Hold with a mean price target of $18.10, implying ~51% upside from current levels.

ticker_oklo.name: Oklo Inc.
ticker_oklo.blurb: Oklo Inc. is a nuclear energy startup developing small fission power plants and advanced fuel technologies. The company operates across multiple business lines including energy generation (Ohio), nuclear fuel recycling (Tennessee), and isotope production (Texas). Oklo aims to commercialize compact nuclear reactors to deliver clean, reliable power to data centers, industrial customers, and remote sites.
ticker_oklo.recent: Oklo recently cleared a significant regulatory or commercial hurdle that drove its stock higher, according to a Wall Street Journal-cited report. The company continues to operate at a loss as it works toward its first commercial reactor deployment, with deepening losses flagged in recent coverage despite investor optimism about its long-term pipeline.

ticker_uuuu.name: Energy Fuels Inc.
ticker_uuuu.blurb: Energy Fuels Inc. is a leading U.S.-based critical minerals company focused on uranium production, rare earth elements (REE), and heavy mineral sands (HMS). The company explores, develops, and operates uranium mines alongside the White Mesa Mill in Utah—the only conventional uranium mill in the United States capable of processing uranium ore and alternative feedstocks. Energy Fuels is also advancing REE separation at the mill, producing oxides from monazite sands to reduce U.S. reliance on Chinese REE supplies. Its vertically integrated model, spanning mining to milling, provides a competitive edge as domestic uranium production gains priority on national security grounds.
ticker_uuuu.recent: Over the 30 days ending mid-May 2026, UUUU climbed approximately +13%, moving from roughly $19.54 to $22.04, driven by rising uranium spot prices, uranium sales exceeding expectations, and reaffirmed 2026 production guidance of up to 2.5 million pounds. Q1 2026 revenue surged 112% year-over-year to $36 million, though EPS came in at -$0.04, missing estimates; net loss nonetheless improved significantly versus the prior-year period. Analyst sentiment strengthened after H.C. Wainwright raised its price target to $29, and broader nuclear energy demand tailwinds supported the stock despite post-earnings volatility.

ticker_leu.name: Centrus Energy Corp.
ticker_leu.blurb: Centrus Energy Corp. is a leading supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry. The company provides enriched uranium, uranium hexafluoride, and related services to utilities and other customers globally. Centrus is also advancing its American Centrifuge technology to produce high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) for next-generation reactors, positioning itself as a key player in the U.S. nuclear fuel supply chain.
ticker_leu.recent: In the past 30 days, Centrus Energy stock has seen increased volatility amid growing interest in nuclear energy as a clean power source. The company has been in the news for its role in developing HALEU fuel for advanced reactors, supported by U.S. government contracts. Price action has been positive, reflecting investor optimism about nuclear fuel demand.

ticker_xe.name: X-Energy, Inc.
ticker_xe.blurb: X-Energy, Inc. is a nuclear reactor technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Rockville, Maryland. Its flagship product is the Xe-100, a small modular reactor (SMR) designed to generate 80 megawatts of electric power or 200 megawatts of thermal output. The company also manufactures TRISO-X fuel, a high-assay low-enriched uranium pebble fuel designed for advanced reactors. With 889 employees and a market capitalization of approximately $12.2 billion, X-Energy is one of the leading pure-play SMR developers in the United States.
ticker_xe.recent: X-Energy completed its IPO on April 24, 2026, making it one of the most closely watched nuclear energy listings of the year. The stock has traded in a range of roughly $29.45–$37.10 since its debut, closing at $30.99 on May 13, 2026 — a decline of 2.36% on the day, with pre-market weakness continuing into May 14. The company's next earnings report is scheduled for May 30, 2026; trailing twelve-month revenue stands at $94.26 million (+12.2% year-over-year) against a net loss of $389.78 million.

ticker_bwxt.name: BWX Technologies, Inc.
ticker_bwxt.blurb: BWX Technologies is a U.S.-based manufacturer of nuclear components, reactors, and nuclear fuel serving government and commercial customers in the United States, Canada, and internationally. The company operates through two segments — Government Operations and Commercial Operations — producing precision naval nuclear components, reactor systems, critical nuclear assemblies, and uranium downblending services. Founded in 1867 and employing roughly 10,400 people, BWXT is a primary supplier to the U.S. Navy's nuclear propulsion program and is positioned at the intersection of defense and the civilian nuclear renaissance. With a market cap near $19 billion and trailing revenue of $3.4 billion, it is one of the few vertically integrated nuclear technology contractors in North America.
ticker_bwxt.recent: BWXT reported Q1 2026 earnings on May 4, 2026, with trailing twelve-month EPS of $3.75 (+19.4% year-over-year) and net income of $344.6 million (+19.2%), reflecting strong government demand. The stock closed at $206.83 on May 13, 2026, sitting in the upper half of its 52-week range of $106.22–$241.82; market cap has expanded roughly 91% over the trailing year, driven by renewed U.S. nuclear-defense spending and advanced reactor interest. An upcoming ex-dividend date of May 19, 2026 ($1.08 annual dividend) and a consensus analyst Buy rating with a $209.96 price target round out the near-term picture.

ticker_nne.name: NANO Nuclear Energy Inc.
ticker_nne.blurb: NANO Nuclear Energy Inc. is a pre-revenue nuclear energy development company focused on advanced microreactor and small modular reactor (SMR) technologies. Its portfolio includes four reactor concepts: KRONOS (high-temperature gas-cooled reactor), LOKI (compact microreactor for remote applications), ZEUS (solid core battery reactor), and ODIN (low-pressure salt coolant reactor). Beyond reactors, the company is developing a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) fuel processing facility as well as fuel transportation and nuclear consulting businesses. With only 36 employees and no revenue as of its latest filings, NNE is firmly in early-stage development, targeting the emerging market for distributed and off-grid nuclear power.
ticker_nne.recent: As of mid-May 2026, NNE shares traded around $27, well off their 52-week high of $60.87 but above the 52-week low of $18.93, reflecting ongoing volatility consistent with its beta of 5.14. The company's Q1 2026 earnings were scheduled for May 14, 2026, a near-term catalyst watched closely given a trailing net loss of approximately $43.5M and no revenue. Market cap stood near $1.41B, with analyst consensus at Hold and a price target of $29.50.
